title: The Revakhanda of the Skanda Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: The Revākhaṇḍa is the Narmada section of the Skandapurāṇa tradition, transmitted as the Bṛhat Śrīnarmadāpurāṇa; the edition followed here is Oṅkārānanda Giri's (Jñānasatru Prakāśana), and it was input by Jürgen Neuss, whose study of the text established its place beside the Vāyu Purāṇa's Revākhaṇḍa.
description: The Revākhaṇḍa is the Purana of the Narmada: it narrates the origin of the river and the pilgrimage along its banks, the sacred places from Omkareshvara and Maheshvara to the mouth of the river, the vratas and gifts performed there, the greatness of the linga of Omkara, the story of the river's descent and of the sages who bathed in it, and the merit that follows from hearing it. It is a place-Purana, one region's scripture of its river.
historicalContext: The text is a late compilation that belonged to the Narmada's pilgrimage cult, and its transmission shows how a regional place-Purana was attached to the Skandapurāṇa and printed as part of it; Jürgen Neuss's work on the two Revākhaṇḍas separated the Skanda Purāṇa's text from the Vāyu Purāṇa's.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: the 116 chapters and 6,724 verses of the Revākhaṇḍa, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as chapter.verse. GRETIL also publishes the Revākhaṇḍa that the Vāyupurāṇa tradition carries, and the library holds it as its own work.
